title: Start with the user’s task, not the screen
outcome: Turn a vague feature request into a task, context, success condition, and recovery path.
useCase: Feature scoping and UX review for operational workflows.
benefits: Connects interface decisions to outcomes people need.
drawbacks: A task hypothesis still needs observation; a tidy diagram is not user evidence.
version: Web UX · WCAG 2.2 · principles, not magic formulas
cue: Who is trying to do what, under which pressure?

trace.title: User and context
trace.detail: A screen is a means to finish a task. “Add a dashboard” is not yet a task. “Find the oldest urgent ticket and assign it before the shift ends” is. Name the user, their goal, what they already know, and what interrupts them.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Observe one realistic attempt. Where does the person start? How do they identify the right records? What tells them the action finished? What do they do when only 12 of 15 changes succeed?

Write a decision log: observed problem → design choice → expected benefit → check. This keeps a critique from becoming a contest of taste.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Copying a competitor’s layout without the same user/context can add irrelevant controls. Showing a database term can make users guess. A success toast can hide partial failure.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Turn a vague feature request into a task, context, success condition, and recovery path. Explain one example and one failure.
